In this stage, after clicking “Next”, you will have 5 minutes to adjust sliders to the exact middle position. Every slider will be in a randomly chosen initial position and you are asked to adjust the thumb to the middle position, as illustrated below.



{{ if treat == 1}}

At the end of this stage the computer will compare your number of correctly adjusted sliders with the number of sliders the other participant has adjusted correctly. The participant with the higher number of correctly adjusted sliders is the winner of the competition. The winner receives 28 points. The participant with the lower number is the loser of the competition. The loser receives 14 points. If both participants have the same number of correctly adjusted sliders, a random draw decides which participant is the winner, receiving the 28 points and which participant is the loser, receiving the 14 points (think of this as a coin-flip). At the end of stage 2, you will be informed about your own payoff and the payoff of the other participant. The other participant also receives this information.

{{ else }}

At the end of this stage the computer will randomly and with equal chance determine which participant receives 28 points and which participant receives 14 points (think of this as a coin-flip). That is, one of you ends up receiving 28 points while the other ends up receiving 14 points. This does not depend on the number of correctly adjusted sliders by you or the other participant but is randomly determined by the computer. At the end of Stage 2, you will be informed about your own payoff and the payoff of the other participant. The other participant also receives this information.

{{ endif }} If you have read these instructions, please click on “Next” to start the 5 minutes working period.
